title: RBI gold share in India’s forex reserves falls to 13.98% as prices retreat - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
RBI gold holdings remained virtually unchanged, but a sharp fall in global prices reduced gold’s share of India’s foreign exchange reserves. | Photo Credit: iStockphoto

Gold’s share in India’s foreign exchange reserves has fallen below 14 per cent, reaching its lowest level since September 26, 2025, as the international price of the precious metal fell from its January 2026 peak.

Businessline analysis of RBI data shows gold’s share of total foreign exchange reserves climbed from 13.57 per cent on September 26, 2025, to a peak of 19.02 per cent on January 30, 2026. It subsequently declined, falling to 13.98 per cent by November 13, 2026. This represents a 5.04 percentage-point contraction from the January peak.

The physical quantity of gold held by the RBI has remained virtually unchanged. RBI data show holdings of 880.18 tonnes at end-September 2025 and 880.52 tonnes at end-September 2026, an increase of just 0.34 tonnes.

The movement in global gold prices helps explain this. Spot gold rose to a record of $5,417.21 an ounce on January 28, 2026, before experiencing a sharp correction. By November 13, it had fallen to $3,884.49 an ounce.

The sharp rise in gold prices in January was driven by geopolitical uncertainty, concerns about US economic policy and strong investment demand. Gold rose 14 per cent during the month, supported by 120 tonnes of global gold ETF inflows. On January 28, it touched a record high.

However, the rally reversed on January 29–30 after President Donald Trump nominated Kevin Warsh as the next Federal Reserve chair.

Gold received another boost in early March after the West Asia conflict escalated. Prices reached $5,322 an ounce on March 2 as investors sought safe-haven assets. However, rising crude oil prices heightened inflation concerns and reduced expectations of interest-rate cuts. Gold consequently became less attractive as a non-interest-bearing asset.

The subsequent correction gathered momentum. The World Gold Council attributed March’s 11.8 per cent monthly decline to investment deleveraging, global gold ETF outflows of 84 tonnes and liquidation of speculative futures positions.

Recently, rising US Treasury yields and a stronger dollar weighed on prices in September, while speculative selling, portfolio shifts toward bonds, and repricing of Federal Reserve rate expectations contributed to October’s decline.

Consequently, by November 13, spot gold had fallen to $3,884.49 an ounce, nearly 28.3 per cent below its January 28 peak. With the physical quantity of RBI’s gold holdings broadly stable, this price correction has substantially reduced gold’s contribution to the overall valuation of India’s foreign exchange reserves.
